summary.headline: Laurus Labs Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR2,206 crore (CDMO small molecule +86% YoY) with EBITDA margin up to 34.5%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 total income from operations was a record INR2,206 crore, with H1 at INR4,233 crore (+31%). Gross margin held at about 63% and EBITDA rose to INR762 crore (34.5% margin, up 2.7 pp sequentially), with PAT of INR441 crore in Q2. Small molecule CDMO grew 86% YoY to INR875 crore, while affordable medicines grew 15% YoY to INR1,302 crore. Management reiterated its guidance of over 60% gross margin and over 30% EBITDA margin, and kept a INR3,000 crore capex plan for FY27-28, with peptide commercial revenue expected around FY29.

financial_highlights.change: Highest ever quarter; H1 INR4,233 crore, +31% YoY
Margin up 2.7 pp vs previous quarter
+86% YoY in Q2; about +77% in H1
H1 down about 16% vs base cited in July; attributed to campaign phasing

segments.name: Small molecule CDMO
segments.commentary: Q2 sales INR875 crore, +86% YoY; H1 INR1,710 crore, about +77%. Growth driven by late-stage programs and commercial API supplies to global partners.

segments.name: Affordable medicines
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR1,302 crore, +15% YoY; H1 about +13%. Growth from order book expansion with stable ARV and developed market pricing. Cumulative 96 products filed, 92 DMFs filed to date.

segments.name: Laurus Bio
segments.commentary: Q2 sales INR29 crore; H1 INR64 crore. Laurus Bio 4 commercial fermentation facility expected operational by end of CY2026; commercial supplies may start Q1 FY28.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated guidance of over 60% gross margin and over 30% EBITDA margin for the year; declined to guide beyond that.
Capex guided at about INR3,000 crore for FY27 and FY28; about INR1,500 crore per year thereafter based on current understanding.
Peptide commercial revenues expected around FY29 for the newly commissioned capacity; validation batches expected in about 12 to 18 months.
KRKA formulation facility: Phase 1 production blocks to start mid-2027; meaningful revenues expected in FY28-FY29.
Long-term asset turn target of 1.1x (6-year average), versus current 1.0x and peak of 1.4x.
capex_capacity: Solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS) reactor volume over 16,000 liters (about 16 KL); commercial-scale peptide block commissioned, with further expansion underway. LPPS capacity not quantified.
Total small molecule API reactor volume in operation over 9,000 kiloliters.

Fermentation: 5,000 L GMP facility in Bangalore; 200,000 L food/industrial grade in Tumkur; 500,000 L food/industrial grade facility to be operational in the current quarter; GMP fermentation for animal health expected in H2 CY2027.

Acquisitions announced: 60% stake in Canada-based Galenvs Sciences (oligonucleotides and magnetic nanoparticle purification) and majority stake in SI & C Resins (Hyderabad, peptide resins and chromatography media).
Asset turn currently about 1.0x; management cites brownfield Unit 4 and Unit 2 projects as drivers.
demand_pricing: CDMO pipeline: about 125 active projects (management said the figure is dated); management declined to give program-level counts or commercial-stage split.
No significant customer concentration in CDMO; management expects no major destocking or launch-related volume swings over the next 18 to 24 months.
Affordable medicines: API prices stabilised despite geopolitical pressure; supply chain described as resilient.
Q2 sequential revenue gain of about INR200 crore: CDMO contributed about INR40 crore, affordable medicines about INR160 crore.
Export share is majority of sales; domestic share below 20%. Crop science remains miniscule.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin rise sequentially, and is the lower R&D sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 R&D was higher due to ANDA filings, so the change reflects operational leverage on about INR200 crore of extra revenue rather than R&D cuts. H1 R&D was 4.3% of sales.

qa_highlights.question: Capex delivery given slow H1 run-rate, and capex beyond FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated INR3,000 crore for FY27-28 and said investments are on track. Post FY28 it expects about INR1,500 crore a year, which could rise if opportunities arise.

qa_highlights.question: Free cash flow and H1 operating cash flow decline?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said inventory build is regular working capital that should be utilised in the coming quarter. Net debt to EBITDA is about 1x, and management prioritised growth capex over free cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Laurus Bio outlook and reservation terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the facility will be qualified this quarter, trials in Q4 FY27, and commercial supplies from Q1 FY28. Terms of customer capacity reservations and Laurus Bio EBITDA breakeven were not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Peptide commercial timeline and committed capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Commercial revenue expected around FY29; validation batches in 12 to 18 months. Management declined to share how much capacity is customer-committed or capex and asset turn for peptides.

risks_watch: Peptide commercial ramp depends on regulatory approvals and validation; revenue timing (FY29) and utilisation remain unquantified and undisclosed.
Laurus Bio H1 revenue decline and delayed commercial start (Q1 FY28); EBITDA breakeven not disclosed.
Free cash flow pressure from INR3,000 crore capex and inventory build; H1 operating cash flow fell 26% per the analyst.
Asset turn at about 1.0x, below the 1.1x target and the 1.4x peak; new capex may dilute it.
Management withheld many granular metrics (peptide capex, customer counts, validation volumes, cost structure), limiting external modelling.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, margins and capacity build-out, but evasive on granular disclosures. Management declined to quantify peptide capex, customer commitments, commercial timelines, pipeline counts and resin or API cost structure, citing confidentiality and strategy.
key_quotes: We are offering an API, not just fragments.
Business will not come today, it will come tomorrow. So we don't want to spoil partnerships or relationships by taking too much that we cannot handle.
So around INR1,500 crores per year capital expenditure based on the current understanding.
Our customers are asking us to get there. So we're invested.

growth.why: Management reiterated only margin guidance (gross margin >60%, EBITDA >30%) and capex of INR3,000 crore for FY27-28 with no explicit revenue growth figure; H1 revenue is up 31% YoY and Q2 CDMO up 86%, backed by commercial peptide block, Tumkur fermentation and KRKA Phase 1 timelines, but most new capacity lands FY28-FY29.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose 2.7 pp sequentially to 34.5% on about INR200 crore extra revenue (operational leverage), but management only commits to over 30% and R&D is 4.3% of sales with ANDA filings ongoing.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Tumkur 500,000 L fermentation in trial runs and operational this quarter; Laurus Bio 4 facility qualified this quarter with commercial supplies from Q1 FY28; commercial-scale peptide block already commissioned (16,000+ L SPPS); INR3,000 crore capex for FY27-28 reiterated.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Small molecule CDMO grew 86% YoY in Q2 to INR875 crore and affordable medicines 15% to INR1,302 crore, with order book expansion and no major destocking expected over 18-24 months.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Total small molecule API reactor volume over 9,000 KL with brownfield Unit 4 and Unit 2 projects underway and asset turn at 1.0x vs 1.1x target; post-FY28 capex guided at about INR1,500 crore per year, so further sizing is expected but not yet a new headline announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue up 31% YoY and Q2 CDMO up 86%, but management reiterated margin floors only and declined to guide revenue growth beyond that.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gross margin guidance of over 60% and EBITDA margin over 30% reiterated while H1 EBITDA margin is 33.2% and Q2 is 34.5%, giving headroom above the floor.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Laurus Bio commercial supplies from Q1 FY28 and peptide commercial revenue expected around FY29 (validation batches in 12-18 months); 96 products filed and 92 DMFs filed to date in affordable medicines.

rows.label: KRKA formulation Phase 1 production blocks
rows.why: Phase 1 blocks scheduled for mid-2027 with meaningful revenues expected in FY28-FY29.

rows.label: Galenvs Sciences and SI & C Resins acquisitions
rows.why: 60% stake in Canada-based Galenvs (oligonucleotides) and majority stake in SI & C Resins (peptide resins) announced, adding peptide and oligo capabilities.

rows.label: Inventory build and H1 operating cash flow decline
rows.why: H1 operating cash flow fell 26% per the analyst; management expects inventory build to be utilised next quarter, with net debt/EBITDA at about 1.02x vs 1.28x last quarter.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, margins and the INR3,000 crore capex build-out, but evasive on peptide capex, customer commitments, Laurus Bio breakeven and pipeline counts; analysts pressed on margin sustainability, free cash flow and capex delivery.
